text: Last week, a message from Earth took one full day to reach Voyager 1. Nothing we have ever built is farther away.
This is Voyager 1, built from NASA's own 3D model. It launched in September nineteen seventy-seven, and it still talks to us.
Its dish is three point seven metres wide. Its radio sends with about twenty-two watts.
Moving at the speed of light, its signal needs a whole day to get home. A question and its answer take two days.
Then, in November twenty twenty-three, Voyager started sending nonsense.
One memory chip in its flight data computer had failed. About three percent of that memory, gone.
Nobody can fly out there and replace a chip. So the engineers decided to move the code.
No single free spot was big enough. So they cut the code into pieces, and stored each piece in a different place.
On April eighteenth, twenty twenty-four, they sent the first piece. Then they waited for the answer.
Two days later, Voyager made sense again, for the first time in five months.
